intro.title: Build sandboxed code runner safe eval strategy
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a safe, sandboxed code runner that can execute user-provided JavaScript without risking your main application. You'll learn how to use the Function constructor to create isolated execution contexts, which helps prevent access to global variables and dangerous APIs. The core programming concept involves creating a controlled environment (a sandbox) to run untrusted code securely. You'll work with JavaScript's built-in Function constructor and learn strategies to limit its capabilities for safety. By the end, you'll have a basic but functional safe eval strategy that can run code snippets securely.
intro.usecase: This sandboxed code runner pattern is essential for any application that allows users to execute custom code safely. You'll see it in online code playgrounds like CodePen or JSFiddle, where users can write and test JavaScript without compromising the hosting platform. It's also critical in educational platforms like freeCodeCamp or Codecademy, where learners submit code exercises that need isolated evaluation. Additionally, dashboard builders and CMS systems use this approach to safely execute custom widget logic or user-defined formulas without risking the main application's security.
